items.claim: The burden-noun reading of the idols' load at Isa.46.1-Isa.46.2 rather than an oracle header is correct, and the seam into Isa.46.3 rests on a genuine discourse-voice shift.
items.evidence: מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (Isa.46.1, byte tier) sits mid-verse inside third-person narration of idols loaded onto pack animals, not in the verse-initial position that marks the ten header sites of the massa series; the row correctly keeps this burden-noun use apart from the header class and from the mid-verse header-reference class, matching the book's own three-role split for the root. The carry-root catchword running into Isa.46.3 is disclosed as cross-seam cohesion rather than left silent, and is outweighed by the shift from third-person idol-procession description to a first-person divine vocative naming a new addressee -- a legitimate discourse-frame boundary, not an arbitrary cut.
tier_citations: discourse-voice signal (3rd-person to 1st-person vocative, argued from bytes, no non-textual tier)

items.claim: The inclusio bracketing Isa.46.3 and Isa.46.12 is byte-confirmed at the accent-stripped tier, and the row's rejected alternative is the genuinely strongest internal rival, correctly answered.
items.evidence: Isa.46.3 opens שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (byte tier) and Isa.46.12 opens שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י (byte tier); the two differ only in cantillation and collate identical at the accent-stripped tier (accent-stripped, tier named), supporting the row's reading of Isa.46.12 as a bracket-closure inside the same unit rather than a fresh onset. Among this row's own internal imperatives, זִכְרוּ זֹ֖את (Isa.46.8, byte tier) is the strongest candidate rival division, since its cataphoric 'this' pattern most resembles the summons formulas this cluster treats as onset-strength elsewhere (Isa.47.8, Isa.48.1); the row names and answers exactly this rival rather than a weaker one.

items.claim: Reading the redeemer confession at Isa.47.4 as an embedded communal aside rather than an addressee shift is correct, and the row's disclosed rival is a genuine live alternative, not a strawman.
items.evidence: Isa.47.4 shifts to first-person-plural voice ('our Redeemer') between second-person-feminine-singular imperatives addressing Babylon directly on both sides of it (Isa.47.1, Isa.47.5), consistent with an embedded aside rather than a fresh address; the row's rejected alternative -- holding the whole addressee-constant chapter as one unit through Isa.47.15 -- is a real rival given the unbroken addressee, and the row answers it with a named internal pivot rather than dismissing it without grounds.
tier_citations: grammatical-person signal (argued from bytes, no non-textual tier)

items.claim: The formal pivot at Isa.47.8 belongs to a distinct formula-class from the vocative bracket used in the preceding row, and the row's rejected alternative at Isa.47.12 is a genuine rival, correctly answered.
items.evidence: וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי זֹ֤את (Isa.47.8, byte tier) pairs a transition particle with the cataphoric hear-this formula that recurs verse-initially as שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את at Isa.48.1 -- a distinct class from the vocative bracket ('hear me') used inside the previous row -- supporting a fresh-row reading at Isa.47.8. עִמְדִי נָ֤א (Isa.47.12, byte tier) is an imperative onset the row correctly identifies and rejects as a rival split, since it continues the same accusatory address opened at Isa.47.8 rather than introducing a fresh addressee or frame.

items.claim: The Isa.48.1-Isa.48.11 merge is correct: no imperative, vocative, or frame-onset interrupts between the hear-this summons and the row's own close, so the rejected split at Isa.48.3 lacks a tier-1 trigger.
items.evidence: Isa.48.4 through Isa.48.10 is continuous first-person divine declarative speech with no imperative or vocative onset at any verse boundary in that span (checked verse by verse against the pointed text), so the shift in argument content at Isa.48.3, from accusation to predictive-proof, is not accompanied by a formal frame marker of the kind this cluster otherwise treats as seam-bearing. The row's own rejected alternative correctly names this as the strongest available candidate while showing it fails the tier-1 bar the row's actual seams meet.

items.claim: This row's rejected-alternative disclosure omits a candidate seam at least as strong as the one it names, weakening its rival-quality warrant.
items.evidence: Isa.48.14 opens with הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ ('assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear', byte tier), a plural imperative-plus-hear summons of the same formal class this cluster elsewhere treats as sufficient to open a fresh unit -- the hear-this summonses opening the neighboring rows at Isa.47.8 and Isa.48.1, and the singular vocative שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ that opens this very row at Isa.48.12. The row folds Isa.48.14 into continuous content with no examination of it as a rival division point and no addressee-continuity argument offered for passing over it, while it explicitly weighs and rejects a different, later candidate at Isa.48.16. A rival-quality check that names the weaker of two comparable candidates while staying silent on the stronger one is a disclosed-rival gap, not a strawman-rival problem, but it still falls short of this row's own demonstrated standard elsewhere in the cluster (compare the correctly-identified rivals at Isa.46.8 and Isa.47.12 in the neighboring rows).

items.claim: The bare departure imperative at Isa.48.20 marks a genuine register shift from argued speech to enacted proclamation, and the row's cross-book note on Isa.57.21 is byte-accurate and correctly held apart from boundary evidence.
items.evidence: Isa.48.20 opens צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ ('leave Babylon', byte tier), a plural imperative pair carrying no hear-formula, matching the row's own contrast with the teaching-lament register of the preceding row. Collation confirms אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים at Isa.48.22 recurs at Isa.57.21 as אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים, with a different divine-name token (Elohai) substituted for the tetragrammaton, exactly as the row states; the row correctly registers this as cross-part texture in prose only, not as boundary evidence for either verse's own seam, matching the campaign's cross-tradition/metadata discipline for non-adjacent recurrence.

items.claim: This row's device_notes misattributes where its own referent-hold argument appears, naming the wrong field.
items.evidence: The referent-tension discussion (the speaker being addressed as 'Israel' in Isa.49.3 set against the Isa.49.5-Isa.49.6 commissioning that sends the same speaker to Jacob and Israel as though distinct) is stated in this row's own boundary rationale prose, not in its strongest-rejected-alternative text, which instead addresses only a proposed split isolating the complaint from the commissioning. device_notes' claim that the rejected-alternative field carries the referent question misdescribes the row's own structure. The row's underlying discipline is otherwise sound on this point -- it holds both readings open and does not decide the servant referent, meeting the governing constraint for this unit type -- but the cross-field citation itself is inaccurate and should be corrected to point at the boundary rationale.
